title: Surge Forecasting Scratchpad — Weekly
content:
Surge Forecasting Scratchpad — weekly sync (notes-to-self style)
Date: 2026-11-30
Owner: Maya Chen (infra capacity)
Attendees: Maya, Jonah, Priya, Hank (+ async comments from SRE channel)

TL;DR
- Short window surge expected next Wed–Fri due to customer X onboarding test (see INFRA-2247). Forecast peak qps ~+18% in us-west-2; tail-latency risk if no pre-warm.
- Proposed: prewarm pool +10% for us-west-2 on Wed 02:00–14:00 PST; enable regional backfill policy alpha for low-pri jobs.
- Next steps: run quick sim with new weekday-seasonality weighting and check hit-rate for KV-cache. Jonah to run sim by Tue EOD.

Data signals observed (raw):
- baseline avg qps (last 7d) us-west-2: 12.4k
- 95th-percentile hour spikes: 14.6k (one-off), 13.8k (recurring daily evening)
- customer X dry-run (today): sustained 1.9k qps for 40m starting 21:20 PST
- preemption count (GCP preemptible nodes) increased 2.1x under similar load last month

Forecast model notes (sketch):
- Current model: moving-average + time-of-week multiplier. Underweights short-duration enterprise bursts.
- Quick tweak: add 'scheduled-customer-event' flag and exponential decay window (t0..t+3h) to boost short-term forecast.
- Risk: overprovisioning if flag mis-attributed. Mitigate with canary-prewarm (scale up to X nodes, measure, hold).

Hypotheses to test:
1) Adding the event-flag will improve spike capture rate from 62% -> ~82% (measured as fraction of peak QPS captured within 10% margin).
2) Regional backfill of low-priority queues reduces cold-start tail latency by ~12% without increasing cost >3%.
3) Auto-dropping preemptible mix to <20% during predicted surge reduces retries and user-facing errors (empirical eval in sim).

Experiment plan (short):
- Jonah: run fleet-sim branch (#382) with event-flag on 2026-11-30 sim window; inputs: last 30d traces + customer X test pattern. Outcome: forecast hit-rate + provisioning delta. (target: Tue 2026-12-01 18:00)
- Priya: small canary prewarm in us-west-2: +5 dedicated instances @ 02:00–06:00 Wed; collect latency + error rates; rollback if tail-latency worsens. (target: Wed 02:00 run)
- Hank: toggle backfill policy to alpha for low-prio queue on Wed; monitor queue drain and cost. (note: gate is SLA-ok customers only)

Runbook updates (quick scratch):
- Add section: "Short-duration scheduled surges" with decision tree: detect flagged customer event -> evaluate confidence (model score) -> if >0.7, trigger canary prewarm -> if canary tail-latency improves, scale to target -> monitor 5min buckets -> scale down after 3 consecutive buckets below threshold.
- Add fallback: if prewarming exhausted and latency > SLA, route to secondary region (us-east-1) with model-variant fallback (lower-cost quantized variant).

Operational checklist for Wed run (owner tags):
- [Maya] Add event flag for customer X in forecasting config (done by 02:00 Mon)
- [Jonah] Run sims and post results to #infra-capacity (by Tue EOD)
- [Priya] Prepare canary instance template + alerts (latency >= 200ms 5m over baseline)
- [Hank] Prepare backfill toggle with circuit-breaker (auto-off if CPU saturation > 85%)
- [Maya] Notify CS/solutions-eng of potential degraded perf window and planned mitigation (email + slack)

Observed anomalies / notes from past week (for context):
- We saw odd KV-cache eviction patterns around 2026-11-22 that correlate with a sudden multi-customer prefix cache churn. Investigate whether recent model rollouts changed prompt-prefix lengths. Ticket: INFRA-2301.
- Cost note: last month's prewarming for marketing campaign increased bill by ~4.2% but avoided a 2.3% increase in error budget for affected customers. Need clearer cost-vs-availability acceptance criteria.

Decisions made (quick):
- Approve alpha backfill toggle for low-priority jobs during scheduled surge windows (Hank to own rollback conditions).
- Approve canary prewarm for us-west-2 Wed window (+5 instances) — temporary, re-evaluate after telemetry.

Open questions / risks:
- How to avoid overfitting the forecast to customer-provided schedules? (need manual override + expiry)
- Preemptible node behavior: if cloud provider increases preemptions, our prewarm + backfill model might not hold. Add preemption signal into model.
- Cross-region replication time for large model variants may increase failover latency; measure model artifact warm-up time if routing to secondary is used.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- If Jonah's sim shows >12% overprovision for 1h windows, consider adding cool-down decay to prevent flip-flop scaling.
- Need a neat dashboard tile: "scheduled events capture rate" (goal >80%).

Meeting cadence & follow-ups:
- Weekly sync same time Wed 10:30 but add 15-min prebrief on Tue if sim results delayed.
- Post mortem draft if any run causes customer-visible error >1% for >10m.

Useful links / artifacts:
- INFRA-2247 (customer X onboarding)
- INFRA-2301 (kv-cache churn investigation)
- GH PR fleet-sim #382 (forecast event-flag)
- Slack thread: #infra-capacity "customer-x surge" pinned messages

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya
summary: Scratchpad for short-duration surge forecasting: data signals, planned canary prewarm in us-west-2, backfill alpha, sim tasks, and runbook-first changes. Targets: test event-flag in sim and execute canary Wed 02:00–06:00.
